extraction.name: MathVista
extraction.description: MathVista is a benchmark designed to combine challenges from diverse mathematical and visual tasks. It consists of 6,141 examples, derived from 28 existing multimodal datasets involving mathematics and 3 newly created datasets (i.e., IQTest, FunctionQA, and PaperQA). Completing these tasks requires fine-grained, deep visual understanding and compositional reasoning.
extraction.creator: Pan Lu, Hritik Bansal, Tony Xia, Jiacheng Liu, Chunyuan Li, Hannaneh Hajishirzi, Hao Cheng, Kai-Wei Chang, Michel Galley, Jianfeng Gao
extraction.publisher: UCLA, University of Washington, Microsoft Research, Redmond
extraction.citeAs: Pan Lu, Hritik Bansal, Tony Xia, Jiacheng Liu, Chunyuan Li, Hannaneh Hajishirzi, Hao Cheng, Kai-Wei Chang, Michel Galley, Jianfeng Gao. MathVista: Evaluating Mathematical Reasoning of Foundation Models in Visual Contexts. ICLR 2024.
extraction.rai:dataCollection: MathVista incorporates 28 existing multimodal datasets, including 9 math-targeted question answering (MathQA) datasets and 19 VQA datasets. In addition, three new datasets (IQTest, FunctionQA, PaperQA) were created. For MathQA datasets, each source dataset is limited to up to 400 examples to ensure balanced representation. For VQA datasets, heuristic rules were used to automatically select examples likely to involve mathematical reasoning from a large pool of candidates, yielding 4,949 VQA-format examples. Expert annotators manually labeled these examples to determine if they involve mathematical reasoning using majority voting, finalizing 2,739 examples. The three new datasets were manually annotated by graduate students in STEM fields and refined through a rigorous review process.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Data sources include 28 existing multimodal datasets (9 MathQA datasets and 19 VQA datasets) and 3 newly created datasets. MathQA datasets include sources for geometry problem solving, math word problems with visual contexts, and textbook question answering on college curricula. VQA datasets were reviewed from more than 70 datasets, selecting 19 that contain math-related instances and are publicly available. New datasets include IQTest (228 examples from puzzle test figures on online learning platforms), FunctionQA (400 examples emphasizing functional plots and algebraic reasoning), and PaperQA (107 examples from papers released in August 2023 on Huggingface).
extraction.rai:dataCollectionTimeframe: Papers released in August 2023 were used for PaperQA dataset. The overall collection process timeframe is not explicitly stated.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: For VQA datasets, heuristic rules were designed to automatically select examples likely to involve mathematical reasoning. Examples with numeric answers or those containing quantity words were selected. This automatic filtration yielded 4,949 VQA-format examples. Each source dataset was limited to up to 400 examples to ensure balanced representation. The dataset was divided into two subsets: testmini (1,000 examples) and test (5,141 examples). A sampling strategy was adopted to ensure testmini closely resembles the distribution of the whole set.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Three expert annotators manually labeled VQA examples to determine if they involve mathematical reasoning, using majority voting. For the three new datasets (IQTest, FunctionQA, PaperQA), all questions were manually annotated by graduate students in STEM fields and further refined through a rigorous review process. A two-step process was employed: initially, each dataset was independently annotated by three reviewers, resulting in a high inter-annotation consistency rate of 99.2%. Discrepancies were resolved through discussion among the entire review team. Metadata annotations include question type, answer type, language, source, category, task, grade level, and visual context. Coarse labels of mathematical reasoning were automatically obtained from source dataset details, with expert annotators manually labeling mathematical reasoning categories for 1,000 examples to verify quality.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationPlatform: A custom annotation tool was developed, with GUI illustrated in the paper (Figure 23 for new datasets, Figure 22 for mathematical reasoning labeling, Figure 24 for mathematical reasoning skills).
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: For VQA dataset labeling, three expert annotators labeled examples with a Fleiss Kappa score of 0.775, indicating substantial consistency. Among 736 newly collected questions, only 6 exhibited disagreements in annotated answers, which were resolved through discussion. For automatic annotation of mathematical reasoning categories, 94.1% of examples from automatic and human annotations had the exact same set of reasoning types, while 98.79% of individual labels were identical.
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The dataset is divided into testmini (1,000 examples) for model development validation and test (5,141 examples) for standard evaluation. Answer labels for the test set will not be publicly released to prevent data contamination, and an online evaluation platform will be maintained. The authors are committed to maintaining the datasets and refining potential data noise in response to community feedback, and evolving the leaderboard in response to new models.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: While MathVista encompasses a broad spectrum of tasks and visual contexts, there may be gaps in the representation of certain types of mathematical problems and visuals. The dataset's focus on mathematical reasoning within visual contexts, spanning specific domains like science and college-level math, necessitates a more labor-intensive process for collecting high-quality data. Annotations were sourced from original data providers, resulting in only 85.6% of examples having annotations. Due to the heterogeneity of sources, annotations lack a unified format and structure. The scalability and generalizability of the benchmark to other domains remain a concern.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: MathVista is designed for evaluating mathematical reasoning of foundation models in visual contexts. It can be used for model development validation (testmini subset) or standard evaluation (test subset). The benchmark is intended to facilitate the development of mathematical reasoning systems in visually intensive scenarios and evaluate the research progress of LLMs and LMMs, especially their capabilities in solving rigorous reasoning tasks.
extraction.rai:annotationsPerItem: Three annotators per item for manual labeling of VQA examples and for the newly created datasets.
extraction.rai:annotatorDemographics: Graduate students in STEM fields annotated the three new datasets. For human performance baseline, eligible annotators from Amazon Mechanical Turk must have a satisfactory annotating history, successfully pass qualification examples, and possess a high school degree or higher.
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: EasyOCR was used for OCR text detection. Multimodal Bard was used to generate image captions for augmented LLMs. GPT-4 was used as an answer extractor for evaluation.
